neighbours.label: Fires on the token just before an expected 'perfect' (nobody is / isn't / not / picture- + perfect), i.e. predicts the word 'perfect' or 'perfection' next, mostly in negated or hedged perfectionism contexts
fire: Stop beating yourself up over every little slip, because honestly nobody is perfect, and the sooner you accept that the happier you will be.
She spent the whole weekend arranging the table and the flowers, trying to make the dinner party look picture perfect for her in-laws.
The report was solid and well argued, but let's be honest: the methodology was not perfect and the sample was small.
Our coach kept telling us the same thing before every match. Don't wait until everything is perfect, just get out there and play.
The design of the old bridge was impressive for its time, yet it was hardly a flawless piece of engineering and it needed constant repair.
Perfectionism can paralyze a writer. You don't have to get every sentence right on the first draft, because no first draft is ever perfect.
Take a look at this photo of the lake at sunrise, with the mountains reflected in still water; it really is a postcard perfect morning.
The textbook warns that a measurement is never exact. Real instruments are not ideal, and every reading carries some small error.
quiet: Stop beating yourself up over every little slip, because honestly nobody is watching, and the sooner you accept that the happier you will be.
She spent the whole weekend arranging the table and the flowers, trying to make the dinner party feel warm and welcoming for her in-laws.
The report was solid and well argued, but let's be honest: the methodology section was long and the sample was small.
Our coach kept telling us the same thing before every match. Don't wait until the whistle blows, just get out there and warm up.
The design of the old bridge was impressive for its time, and it was built by a famous engineer who also designed several railway stations.
Procrastination can paralyze a writer. You need to open the document every morning, because a blank page never fills itself.
Take a look at this photo of the lake at sunrise, with the mountains reflected in still water; I took it from the porch of our cabin.
The textbook explains how a measurement is made. The instruments were calibrated on Monday, and every reading was written into the lab notebook.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, random arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Strong activations sit on the token right before a predicted 'perfect' (nobody IS perfect, isn't, picture-perfect, hardly) and the output direction promotes ' perfect'/'ideal' when the - pole is on, so it looks like a next-word-'perfect' predictor with weaker activations on negation/copula tokens in perfectionism contexts. Mix of contexts, so coverage may be partial.
